statement_verbatim:
statement: >-
  Every Coach instance is called "Coach - <project or repo>" in its window or tab label, its session
  title and the first line of every report it writes, so the owner can tell which repository a Coach
  serves.

statement: >-
  Every decision a Coach takes falls into one of four tiers: act alone, act then report, ask the owner
  first, or never. The tier comes from the action's kind and its reach, not from how confident the
  Coach feels that the action is safe.

statement: >-
  Each decision a Coach takes alone (act alone, or act then report) is written to a decision log with the
  request, the tier, the convention that applies and the evidence, in the same step as the action or before it.

statement: >-
  A request that is small, reversible and already covered by an active convention or a standing approval
  is handled by the Coach without asking the owner. The Coach records the decision and reports it in one line.

statement: >-
  When a Coach cannot place an action in one tier, or cannot tell whether it is reversible or stays inside
  its own repository, it applies the higher of the candidate tiers. An action does not drop a tier because
  it looks small.

statement: >-
  A Coach orchestrates work: it grants and routes, checks evidence, validates merge readiness and reviews
  exceptionally. It never edits repository code and never opens a code pull request itself. Code is
  produced by a worker under a brief and a tracked issue.

statement: >-
  A coder who pushes a branch or opens a pull request for a code change puts the tracker issue id in
  the branch name and in the PR body, and keeps the issue status current: In Progress when the work
  starts, Done when its acceptance is met, and an explicit comment when it is blocked.

statement: >-
  A planner extends the local plan binding with the external tracker: before a decomposition is
  ratified, it is bound to a local ATDD issue (planner.plan.confirm-binds-an-issue) and that issue is
  linked to an issue in the configured tracker, so the owner sees the planned code work before any
  repository change starts.

statement: >-
  When an agent meets a situation no active convention covers, or an active convention that misfires,
  it records a convention proposal and continues its assigned work under the conventions that are
  active now. An agent never creates, edits, disables or deletes an active convention itself. A
  proposal carries concrete evidence, names the profile and area the rule belongs to, and is never
  applied to the task in which it was raised. Gaps found by experiments enter through the same path.

statement: >-
  An automatic context handoff MUST fire at most once per threshold crossing, MUST be latched at the
  crossing rather than cancelled by usage read later (Pi may compact first), MUST be dropped only when
  the run was aborted, and MUST stop at a configured hop limit. A failed or cancelled session switch
  MUST keep the record for a manual retry and MUST NOT retry on its own.

statement: >-
  A context handoff record MUST carry only bounded facts: the issue id, the workspace and revision,
  the usage at the threshold crossing, the task text with values under listed credential labels and token
  shapes redacted on a best-effort basis, and explicit `UNKNOWN` markers for anything not known. Redaction
  is list-based and is not general secret safety; it does not make a prompt safe to repeat. It MUST NOT copy the predecessor's own output, and it MUST
  NOT present any claimed completion as evidence. Its grant is stated by reference to the original brief.
  When the handing-off session is a Coach, the record MAY also carry an optional `Coach state` section under
  the same limits.

statement: >-
  A worker escalates one tier only after two failures on the same task, and only after reporting both
  failures with their evidence. Escalation is never silent. A step to `high` or `xhigh` still needs an
  explicit owner request for the named task.

statement: >-
  Briefs, rules, configs and repository files name a tier (`low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`), never a
  model name, a model id or a hard-coded `--model` flag. The configured tiers file is the only place
  where a tier becomes a provider, model and thinking level.

statement: >-
  Agents run only on the subscription provider families configured in the tiers file. Per-token
  providers (anthropic, openai) are never used for agents unless the owner asks for them by name.
  Switching provider family is the owner's call, and the agent asks for it only through its Coach; it is
  never silent. When a family reaches its limit, the agent reports it and stops or waits rather than
  falling back to another provider.

statement: >-
  When an agent launches another agent or a worker, it chooses the model by tier from its role:
  planners, testers, coders and bounded-task operators run on `low`; coordinators and coaches run on `medium`, and
  `high` or `xhigh` are used only on an explicit owner request for a named task. The brief names the
  tier; the tiers file decides the provider, model and thinking level.

statement: >-
  A code change (repository file, CI, deploy/infra or cloud build config) MUST be bound to an issue in
  the configured tracker before its first change. No issue: ask the owner, or create one only with approval.
  The issue id goes in the branch name and PR body; the issue stays current until the work is done.

statement: >-
  With no tracker configured, a code change cannot be bound to a tracker issue: say so explicitly in the
  report and check result. Never report it as tracked, never pass it silently, never invent a tracker or id.

statement: >-
  A repository that still uses a legacy railway term (wagon, train, interlocking, Cargo, WMBT,
  Station Master) migrates it with the mapping table in conventions/legacy-terms.yaml. Prose in a file
  the agent is already editing takes the new term in the same commit. Identifiers (rule ids, paths,
  URN schemes, field keys, code names) migrate as a whole unit with the mechanical tool, because their
  references live in other files and other repositories. Until then the alias keeps the legacy name
  resolving. The vocabulary change is its own commit, and no file keeps both vocabularies after its unit
  is migrated. Advisory until the sunset date (60 days after the release that ships the change), then strict.
